reason: The text repeatedly demonstrates and affirms that Yahweh has taken decisive action to help the Hebrew/Israelite people. Rahab explicitly states 'I know that Yahweh has given you the land' (יָדַ֕עְתִּי כִּֽי־ נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־ הָאָ֑רֶץ). She references Yahweh's past intervention by drying up the Red Sea before them (הוֹבִ֨ישׁ יְהוָ֜ה אֶת־ מֵ֤י יַם־ סוּף֙). The spies themselves confirm that Yahweh has given all the land into their hands (נָתַ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה בְּיָדֵ֖נוּ אֶת־ כָּל־ הָאָ֑רֶץ). The narrative demonstrates Yahweh's intentional support of the Hebrew people through both historical deliverance and present provision of the promised land, indicating that helping the Hebrew people is integral to Yahweh's purpose.
